text:
maria: Heads updeploying our worker that imports @redwood/inference-js. Wrangler build fails at runtime: "ReferenceError: require is not defined" and during runtime `globalThis.process` is undefined. Bundle shows node builtins (fs, net) pulled in. Any pragmatic SDK fixes we can do so a single published package works for Node + CF Workers?

samir: Two pragmatic approaches we use elsewhere: 1) Add a tiny edge-specific entrypoint you can import (`@redwood/inference-js/edge`) and keep node/full-featured entrypoint for Node; or 2) keep one package but make node-only code dynamically imported behind runtime guards so bundlers don't include it. Both require package.json exports to be explicit.

maria: What's a recommended exports layout that works with esbuild/wrangler/vite?

kevin: Example we've used (slightly different than the usual):
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "node": "./dist/index.node.cjs",
    "default": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "edge": "./dist/index.edge.mjs"
  },
  "./edge": {
    "default": "./dist/index.edge.mjs"
  }
}
```
This way: Node-aware bundlers pick `node`, browsers/ESM pick `default`, and consumers who want to be explicit can `import '@redwood/inference-js/edge'`. Note not all bundlers honor `edge` condition; add the `/edge` subpath for clarity.

jena: Important SDK code changes too: remove direct references to Buffer, process.env, and sync fs in the main code path. Use Web APIs when possible: TextEncoder/TextDecoder, globalThis.atob/Uint8Array for base64, and crypto.subtle for HMACs. For node-only helpers, create a file `node-only.js` and only import it dynamically: `if (typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.versions?.node) { await import('./node-only.js') }`. That prevents static bundlers from pulling node shims.

samir: If you must support Buffer API surface, add a tiny portable shim in the edge bundle that implements only the methods we need (fromBase64/toBase64) using atob/btoa and TextEncoder. Avoid pulling the full buffer polyfill (huge).

maria: Types are tripping users. If we add an `/edge` entrypoint how to make types friendly for TS consumers?

kevin: Two options: 1) Keep a single `types` entry pointing at `dist/index.d.ts` that covers both runtimes (preferable). 2) Ship `index.edge.d.ts` and document import `@redwood/inference-js/edge` for edge usage. If you need to map automatically, `typesVersions` can help older TS but is brittle. Simpler: set `types: "./dist/index.d.ts"` and keep declarations runtime-agnostic (avoid `/// <reference types="node"/>` in the base .d.ts).

jena: CI suggestion: add a lightweight integration that runs esbuild with `platform: 'browser'` targeting the edge entrypoint to catch accidental CJS/node deps before release. We add that as a GH action matrix job (node vs edge bundle check).

edge-ci-bot: build error on feature/worker-shim: "Could not resolve \"fs\" from \"dist/index.node.cjs\"" at 2026-03-22T15:01:03Z

maria: OK action items: Kevin: draft PR adding `dist/index.edge.mjs` and exports update. Samir: add dynamic-import guards around node-only helpers and small buffer/base64 shim. Jena: docs snippet for wrangler/esbuild/vite and TS import examples. I'll test `import '@redwood/inference-js/edge'` as a stopgap.

samir: Also recommend SDK expose `clientOptions.fetch` passthrough so callers can set `headers: { 'x-idempotency-key': id }` and `retry: { retries: 0 }` from the worker runtime to avoid duplicate side-effects on CF 5xx/520s.

maria: Thanks all 44d Will follow up on the PR comments."
